source.title: On Structure and Open Problems in Topological Theories Coupled to Topological Gravity

accepted.question_text: In a two-dimensional topological matter theory coupled to topological gravity, Q-exact terms in the action need not decouple because boundaries of the moduli space contribute anomalously. The paper states that this nondecoupling creates problems in defining topological gravity for massive topological theories, and later explains that the theory is well behaved for conformal regulators but that some theories may not admit such a regulator. Determine how topological gravity should be defined for massive topological theories in this setting, including what replaces a conformal regulator when no such regulator exists.
accepted.context_brief: Defining topological gravity for massive topological theories

evidence.quote: This nondecoupling in the action of the theory is connected with the existence of boundaries of the moduli space and leads to problems in defining the topological gravity for massive topological theories.

Therefore, below we will consider only conformal regulators. If for some theories it is impossible to find such a regulator (this happens, for example, in topological sigma models of type A on manifolds with non-zero first Chern class) it seems that this theory should be considered in the asymptotically conformal limit, i.e., when the trace of G is very small and we can neglect it.

accepted.question_text: Let H be the space of observables in a topological theory coupled to topological gravity, filtered by gravitational descendants, and let J be the ring of observables in the underlying topological matter theory. The paper describes two preferred sections from J into H: one section is obtained from a massive deformation of the theory by selecting observables that generate exactly zero-energy states, and another section is defined by requiring the contact-term connection on the bundle of observables over the deformation space of theories to be flat, i.e. to be a good section. Is the section obtained from making the theory massive itself a good section, equivalently do the two preferred sections coincide?
accepted.context_brief: Conjectural coincidence of preferred sections in the descendant filtration

evidence.quote: One preferred section comes from comparing conformal theory with its massive deformation [12], and another appears [11] in the expression for a fiat connection. We conjecture that these two sections coincide.
Conjecture. The section Urn(s) defined by making a theory massive is a good section.
